title: Extending Bench-2-CoP: Where Do Loss-of-Control Capabilities Have Zero Benchmark Coverage?

original_idea.body:
# Extending Bench-2-CoP: Where Do Loss-of-Control Capabilities Have Zero Benchmark Coverage?

**Problem:** Bench-2-CoP found loss-of-control capabilities receive zero coverage in a 195k-question corpus; the paper doesn't characterize what a minimal benchmark for these categories would look like.

**Direction:** Isolate zero-coverage cells in the EU AI Act systemic-risk taxonomy, construct a small proof-of-concept probe set per cell from public agentic tasks, score an open model, report whether the gap is definitional vs genuine absence.

**Why it matters:** Directly attacks the regulatory blind spot on the highest-stakes capabilities. Single GPU.

**Relevant context:** Extends arXiv:2508.05464.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: building probes for zero-coverage loss-of-control capabilities targets a >1yr critical pathway major orgs prioritize.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Assemble small probe sets from public tasks + LLM-as-judge scoring; guided and tractable.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused (20-50 item probe sets for zero-coverage cells) though spanning several cells.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Neglected long-horizon loss-of-control capabilities labs deprioritize; open model, no proprietary data.

low_compute.reasoning: LLM-as-judge scoring on an open model; single mid GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Bench-2-CoP maps the gap; building minimal probes for it is the open extension.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: The gap is mapped; constructing minimal probe sets is the open extension.
